engines.title: Engines
engines.description: An engine is the endpoint that generates the tokens. The agent system (body) — its tools, permissions and sessions — stays exactly the same; only the model provider behind it changes.
engines.usageHint: Once a key is stored, pick "Claude engine on <engine>" from the model picker in a chat. The chat always shows which engine it is running on.
engines.endpointLabel: Endpoint this engine is called on
engines.storedNote: Stored encrypted for your account only. Replace it by saving a new one.
engines.usageHintOpenCode: Once a key is stored, pick the engine's model (for example a "glm/…" entry) from the model picker in a chat.

cell.claudeNative: The engine Claude Code ships with, on the account already signed in here.
cell.claudeGlm: Runs today: verified end to end on this machine, and the chat picker switches to it.
cell.claudeKimi: The endpoint is wired and the code path is live — all that is missing is a Moonshot key.
cell.claudeDeepseek: Deliberately not enabled as an engine. Widening the axis to it is an owner decision, not a repair.
cell.claudeZen: Zen exposes no Anthropic-compatible endpoint, so the Claude body cannot be pointed at it.
cell.opencodeZen: OpenCode's own engine. The path works; it bills against a Zen balance.
cell.opencodeGlm: Runs today: the carrier returns real tokens through our governed provider block.
cell.opencodeAnthropic: API key only. Passing a personal Claude subscription through OpenCode is forbidden outright.
cell.opencodeKimi: Catalogued upstream; needs a Moonshot key.
cell.opencodeDeepseek: Catalogued upstream; needs a DeepSeek key.
cell.codexAnthropic: Codex speaks only the Responses protocol, and Anthropic does not serve it.
cell.codexGlm: z.ai serves no Responses endpoint, and upstream closed the integration request as not planned.
cell.codexKimi: Moonshot answers 404 on /v1/responses — measured. Closed at the vendor, not pending.
cell.codexDeepseek: Same reason: no Responses endpoint to point Codex at.
cell.codexZen: Zen does expose /responses, but this pair has never been run end to end.
cell.kimiNative: Its own engine. A 402 here is the engine billing, not the body — the body runs without it.
cell.kimiGlm: Proven on the terminal, environment only. Inside nassaj it waits on its config guard — no launch before the guard.
cell.kimiZen: Catalogued; bills against a Zen balance.
cell.agyClosed: Antigravity resolves its own model inside its CLI and accepts no external engine.
cell.cursorClosed: Cursor resolves its own model server-side and accepts no external engine.
cell.hermesUnverified: Hermes has its own model layer; no engine pair has been examined.

Capped to workspace-write with network access OFF, same ceiling as Accept Edits — full disk/network access is available only if the operator has explicitly enabled it for this deployment (off by default). Use with caution.

technicalInfo.default: sandboxMode=workspace-write, approvalPolicy=untrusted, network access OFF. Trusted commands: cat, cd, grep, head, ls, pwd, tail, git status/log/diff/show, find (without -exec), etc.
technicalInfo.acceptEdits: sandboxMode=workspace-write, approvalPolicy=never, network access OFF. All commands auto-execute within project directory.
technicalInfo.bypassPermissions: sandboxMode=workspace-write, approvalPolicy=never, network access OFF — the SAME ceiling as Accept Edits on this deployment. sandboxMode=danger-full-access (real full disk/network access) is reachable only when the operator has explicitly set the CODEX_ALLOW_FULL_ACCESS flag for the whole deployment; it is off by default on the fleet.
technicalInfo.overrideNote: You can override this per-session using the mode button in the chat interface.

toggle.title: Dangerous tier — Run any command
toggle.description: Selecting this tier in the matrix above is not enough — you must arm the main switch here. Turning it off immediately drops «Run any command» from all roles.
toggle.warning: This feature allows running any shell command on the server with the service user's privileges. There is no allowlist — the only safeguard is your personal, character-by-character review of each command before pressing Execute. A single wrong or unauthorized command can corrupt data or take the server down.
